question: When the price of a commodity increased by 23%, a family reduced its consumption in such a way that the expenditure on it was only 5% more. By what percentage has the family reduced the consumption of the commodity (correct to one decimal place)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial price and initial expenditure both be 100.

New Price = 100 + 23 = 123, and New Expenditure = 100 + 5 = 105.

Reduction in consumption % = [(New Price − New Expenditure) ÷ New Price] × 100

⇒ [(123 − 105) ÷ 123] × 100 = (18 ÷ 123) × 100 ≈ 14.6%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.6%.**
